components.gap: Barwise Ch. I sec. 1 (pp. 3-13): the definitions (logic, first-order thesis, abstract completeness, strong/countable compactness, L(Q_alpha), L_kappa_lambda) and the results on undefinability, L(Q0) and (omega,<), L(Q0) not r.e., L(Q1) expressive facts, the L_omega1omega definition of Q0, the L(Q0) Beth failure and the second-order failures are present with proofs; but not every source claim and example has its exact hypotheses and complete proof: (a) the L(Q0)-definability of torsion groups, finitely generated groups and finite-dimensional vector spaces (p. 8) is stated as not proved (body 301-306); (b) Mostowski's theorem that a logic of finite syntax in which finiteness is definable has implicitly but not explicitly definable notions (p. 10) is not proved in its general form (body 340-342, 388-393); (c) the results Barwise reports from other work (Vaught's two-cardinal route to L(Q1) completeness, Hanf on compact L_kappa_lambda, Lopez-Escobar, Moschovakis/Svenonius, incomparability of Keisler's probability logic with first-order logic, Rabin's tree theorem, Shelah's four second-order quantifiers, Erdos-Gillman-Henriksen and its partial-isomorphism form) are reported without proof (body 233-253, 332-352, 411-431).

Barwise Ch. I sec. 2 (pp. 13-22): the Lindstrom bridge, interpolation/separation/Delta-closure, boundedness of countably compact regular logics, Hanf existence and the open-question warning are present with proofs, but not every source claim has its complete proof: (a) failure of Robinson's consistency property for L_omega1omega (p. 16; body 489-491); (b) Delta-closure strictly weaker than interpolation, and existence of the least Delta-closed extension Delta(L) (p. 18; body 524-527); (c) Robinson's consistency property equivalent to compactness plus interpolation for logics with few symbols (p. 16; body 536-539); (d) first-order logic characterized by the Lowenheim-Skolem theorem plus boundedness by omega (p. 18; body 572-578); (e) the reported external results (Delta(L(Q0)) = hyperarithmetic fragment of L_omega1omega; L(Q0) bounded by omega_1^CK; L_omega1omega bounded by omega_1; unboundedness of L_omega1omega1 and of the game logic; h(L) = beth_lambda for L(Q0), L_omega1omega, L_kappa_omega; failure of interpolation for L(Q1); the weakly/strongly compact, measurable and Vopenka characterizations) are reported without proof (body 524-539, 572-627).

Barwise Ch. I sec. 3 (pp. 22-23) is programmatic; the body reproduces the omitted topics (computer-language semantics, human languages), the static-objects shortcoming, the treatment of inference, the paucity of completeness theorems and the closing thesis, but omits source claims: that a unified view of logic and semantics will need a framework encompassing both fields; the speech-act point (Austin) that the use of language to effect change (side effects) is left out by traditional model theory and distinguishes computer-language semantics; and the positive programme (getting at the logic of the concepts mathematicians use, finding applications, isolating new concepts) with Barwise's stated uncertainty about which particulars will last.
